title: Two-Dimensional Shapes
introduction: Learn two-dimensional shapes through explanations and practice.
definition: A two-dimensional shape is flat. Polygons have straight sides; circles have curved boundaries. A vertex is a corner where two sides meet.

visuals.label: Square
visuals.alt: Square — 4 equal sides and 4 right angles.

visuals.label: Circle
visuals.alt: Circle — No straight sides or vertices.

examples.question: Count the sides and vertices of a triangle.
steps: A triangle has three straight sides.
The sides meet at three vertices.

examples.question: Compare a square and a rectangle.
steps: A square also has four equal sides.
examples.answer: A square is a special rectangle.

exercises.question: How many vertices does a triangle have?
exercises.solution: A triangle has three corners where its three sides meet.

exercises.question: How many sides does a pentagon have?
exercises.solution: A pentagon is a polygon with five straight sides.

exercises.question: How many sides does a hexagon have?
exercises.solution: A hexagon is a polygon with six straight sides.

exercises.question: Name the shape with four equal sides and four right angles.
exercises.solution: A square has four equal straight sides and four right angles.

exercises.question: How many straight sides does a circle have?
exercises.solution: A circle has a curved boundary, not a straight side.

summary: A two-dimensional shape is flat. Polygons have straight sides; circles have curved boundaries. A vertex is a corner where two sides meet.
